findings.problem: test_ac7_fail_fast_on_typeerror asserts that the first matching document is updated before the TypeError aborts the update. This is only true with MemoryStorage, whose read() returns the live storage dict so the in-place mutation leaks into storage even though Table._update_table never writes when the updater raises. With the default JSONStorage the update is rolled back entirely, so the test encodes storage-dependent, accidental behaviour and would fail with the default storage.
findings.evidence: JSONStorage probe: 'raised: Field \'tags\' is not a list' then "doc1: {'project': 'x', 'id': 1}" (unchanged); MemoryStorage probe: "docs after: [{'id': 1, 'tags': ['x']}, ...]"; MemoryStorage aliasing confirmed: mutating s.read()['_default']['1']['a'] changed s.read() to {'a': 99}

findings.problem: PR bundles unrelated changes to the repository's agent harness (context compaction, ADR-014) into a library feature PR; these are not exercised by the pytest suite (pytest.ini testpaths = tests).

summary: The append operation itself correctly implements all issue requirements and the full suite passes, but the PR's fail-fast test asserts storage-dependent partial-update semantics that only hold with MemoryStorage and contradict the all-or-nothing behaviour under the default JSONStorage.
